rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing the simplest configuration (rna_only with singleprofile and PCA encoder). This clarifies the baseline performance of RNA-only models and isolates the effect of RNA representation, providing critical initial data to inform subsequent decisions.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (singleprofile, RNA-only with PCA) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile (config_002) improves performance while keeping RNA encoder and aggregation method consistent. It isolates the effect of profile setting, a key design choice, and directly compares singleprofile vs multiprofile with minimal changes, providing critical insight into whether multimodal or multiprofile approaches are beneficial.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping multiprofile and avgpool) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile setup with exploration of encoder choices, which are critical design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong baseline, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploitation (building on a proven RNA-only setup) and exploration (testing if image data improves performance), while keeping other parameters consistent to attribute any gains to the addition of image modality.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.65). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer in this high-performing setup clarifies the impact of aggregation. It isolates the effect of aggregation while keeping other key factors (model setting, profile setting, RNA encoder) consistent, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with transformer aggregation (config_006: 0.653) outperform others. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (config_006) to scgpt while keeping transformer aggregation and multiprofile settings isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether newer encoders (scgpt) improve performance compared to scvi_n200 in this context.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests whether combining this strong RNA representation with image data (resnet50) using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion can further improve performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while leveraging proven RNA and aggregation choices, addressing the key uncertainty about whether multimodal approaches can surpass rna_only models.

Existing evidence shows that config_033 (multimodal, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.713). The uncertainty lies in whether the aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool) significantly impacts performance. Testing config_031 (same RNA/image encoders, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) isolates the effect of aggregation, a critical design choice. This comparison helps validate if the current best's aggregation method is optimal, balancing exploitation of existing success with exploration of key hyperparameters.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced image encoder) further improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. This addresses a key uncertainty about image encoder effectiveness while building on the promising multimodal setup.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more complex model) while keeping the image encoder and aggregation method the same (transformer) could improve performance. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which remains uncertain despite scvi_n200's strong performance in rna_only settings. It balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key design decision.
